WEST BENGAL FIRE SERVICES ISSUES ULTIMATUM TO TOP KOLKATA PUJA CLUBS OVER SAFETY VIOLATIONS
KOLKATA — 

In a major development following inspections by a high-power state committee, the West Bengal Fire & Emergency Services (South Kolkata Division) has issued strict compliance notices to prominent Durga Puja organizers—including Chetla Agrani Club, Tridhara Durgotsav, and Ballygunge Cultural Association.

KEY DIRECTIVES & COMPLIANCE MANDATES

 Immediate Lighting Upgrades:
 Organizers are directed to install adequate lighting across pandal premises immediately to prevent dark zones and ensure visibility for crowd management.

 Enhanced Ventilation Systems:
 Mandatory installation of sufficient fans and air conditioning units inside pandals to prevent overcrowding and suffocating conditions.

 Dismantling of Unauthorized Commercial Structures:
 The inspection team identified clusters of temporary commercial structures erected adjacent to pandals in violation of Section 23A of the West Bengal Fire Services (WBFS) Act, 1950.
 The presence of LPG cylinders in makeshift stalls adjacent to pandals constructed with highly flammable materials was flagged as a critical safety hazard.

STRICT DEADLINE ISSUED

 Compliance Deadline: 8:00 PM TODAY (October 18, 2026).
 Mandatory Action: All unauthorized temporary structures and hazardous stalls must be dismantled immediately, and compliance reports submitted directly to local fire stations by the deadline.@CNNnews18 @WBPolice

note_tweet.text:
I’m a big-time pandal hopper. Durga Puja evenings are something I look forward to every year. ❤️

Today, I got ready and stepped out to visit Ahiritola, Kumartuli, Chorbagan, Chaltabagan and other nearby pandals.

After visiting just two pujas, it started raining. I took a cab back home. When we passed near Chorbagan’s main entrance, I saw police personnel and civic volunteers. The rain had kept the crowd relatively thin, and for a moment, I thought of going back.

But with the rain and the difficulty of finding a cab, I decided to return home.

And then I saw the news.

Completely shattered. Heartbroken. Unable to process what happened.

I keep thinking… if it hadn’t rained, would I have still been there? Would I have been standing among those people?

There are so many thoughts running through my mind. So many unanswered questions. A strange, unsettling void that’s difficult to explain.

We go out to celebrate Maa Durga, to seek blessings, to create memories with our loved ones. Nobody steps out expecting that a festive evening could turn into their last.

People getting injured is heartbreaking enough. Losing lives while visiting a Durga Puja pandal is simply too devastating to comprehend.

Life is frighteningly unpredictable. Sometimes, a little rain, a delayed cab, or a small decision to return home can change everything.

Tonight, my heart goes out to every family that has lost a loved one and to everyone affected by this tragedy.

May they find the strength to endure this unimaginable pain. 🙏

Some festive evenings leave us with memories. Others leave us questioning how fragile life really is.

Om Shanti. 🙏

Diplomats and ambassadors from over a dozen countries, including Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Australia and others, visited iconic Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata this week.
Hosted by the Indian Chamber of Commerce under its “Kolkata Connect: Connecting Nations Through Culture” initiative, the delegation toured prominent pandals such as Alipore Sarbojonin, Ballygunge Cultural Association and Rajdanga Amra Sabai Club.
Several envoys described the experience as remarkable, highlighting the festival’s artistic creativity, devotion and community spirit.
This growing international participation underscores Durga Puja’s rising global stature as a UNESCO-recognised Intangible Cultural Heritage, reflecting India’s soft-power outreach and cultural diplomacy.
